levels.speed: Five measured throughput positions: stealth, stealth-16, balanced, fast, max. Conditions differ: fast and max improve on balanced only with raised host TCP ceilings. These are choices, not a universal speed score.
levels.security: Data per directional key epoch: 4 for 1 MiB, 3 for 4 MiB, 2 for 16 MiB, 1 for 64 MiB. Algorithms and mandatory rotation do not change.
levels.stealth: Window, credit-return and idle-rotation settings only: 4 keeps the default 4 MiB budget, two credit returns and idle rotation off. Lower levels enlarge windows or add credit records, and fast and max add idle rekey exchanges. No classifier result is implied; changing the epoch also changes rekey frequency.

coupling.distance: sum of absolute differences on the two untouched axes
coupling.constraint: keep the moved axis at the requested level
coupling.custom_start: Keep custom limits until explicit selection of a combination. Start sliders at that selected combination.

epoch-comparison.conditions: One host, one session, one download, loss-free emulated RTTs of 40, 100 and 200 ms, 6 MiB host TCP ceilings. Six 12-second samples per condition, tail-rate medians. Both peers use the selected limits.
epoch-comparison.limitation: Emulated paths only. Not a real-path speed or stealth claim.

window-comparison.conditions: One host, one session, one download, loss-free emulated RTTs of 40, 100 and 200 ms, host TCP ceilings raised to 64 MiB. Both peers use the selected limits.
window-comparison.limitation: A separate run from epoch-comparison. Host ceilings and the software emulator limit results. Not a real-path speed or stealth claim.
